Chaotic genetic structure and past demographic expansion of the invasive gastropod Tritia neritea in its native range, the Mediterranean Sea 
To better predict population evolution of invasive species in introduced areas it is critical to identify and understand the mechanisms driving genetic diversity and structure in their native range. Here, we combined analyses of the mitochondrial COI gene and 11 microsatellite markers to investigate both past demographic history and contemporaneous genetic structure in the native area of the gastropod Tritia neritea , using Bayesian skyline plots (BSP), multivariate analyses and Bayesian clustering. The BSP framework revealed population expansions, dated after the last glacial maximum. The haplotype network revealed a strong geographic clustering. Multivariate analyses and Bayesian clustering highlighted the strong genetic structure at all scales, between the Black Sea and the Adriatic Sea, but also within basins. Within basins, a random pattern of genetic patchiness was observed, suggesting a superimposition of processes involving natural biological effects (no larval phase and thus limited larval dispersal) and putative anthropogenic transport of specimens. Contrary to the introduced area, no isolation-by-distance patterns were recovered in the Mediterranean or the Black Seas, highlighting different mechanisms at play on both native and introduced areas, triggering unknown consequences for species’ evolutionary trajectories. These results of Tritia neritea populations on its native range highlight a mixture of ancient and recent processes, with the effects of paleoclimates and life history traits likely tangled with the effects of human-mediated dispersal.

nodes.label: Limax marginatus
nodes.description: Terrestrial mollusk species used in the in vitro and in vivo odor-aversion conditioning experiments.

nodes.label: Limax
nodes.description: Genus of terrestrial mollusks containing Limax marginatus and possessing the procerebrum olfactory center.

nodes.label: Odor-aversion conditioning
nodes.description: Differential conditioning paradigm in which an odor is paired with an electrical unconditioned stimulus to induce odor avoidance responses.

nodes.label: Odor learning
nodes.description: Acquisition of odor-related memory or aversion by isolated Limax brain preparations.

nodes.label: Avoidance behavior
nodes.description: Withdrawal or escape response elicited by aversively conditioned or innately aversive odors.

nodes.label: Procerebrum
nodes.description: Olfactory center of Limax containing ongoing synchronized network oscillations and receiving olfactory input.

nodes.label: PC network oscillation frequency
nodes.description: Frequency of synchronized local field potential network oscillations in the Limax procerebrum.

nodes.label: Parietal nerves
nodes.description: Nerves projecting to the mantle muscle and carrying motor output associated with odor-induced mantle shortening.

nodes.label: Mantle muscle shortening
nodes.description: Shortening of the mantle muscle observed during withdrawal from aversively conditioned odors and other repellent odors.

nodes.label: Aversively conditioned odors
nodes.description: Originally attractive odors that were paired with a noxious electrical stimulus and subsequently elicited avoidance responses.

nodes.label: Innately aversive odors
nodes.description: Odors such as onion and garlic that elicited avoidance-related neural and behavioral responses without conditioning.

nodes.label: PC
nodes.description: Neural olfactory-center structure referred to as PC in the discussion of network oscillation and odor processing.

nodes.label: PC network oscillation
nodes.description: Oscillatory neural activity in the PC associated in the text with olfactory processing and modulated experimentally by acetylcholine.

nodes.label: Odor discrimination
nodes.description: Olfactory processing involving discrimination between closely related odors and between aversive and attractive odors.

nodes.label: Posterior cerebral serotonergic cell
nodes.description: Identifiable serotonergic neuron abbreviated p-CSC, whose discharges release serotonin in the tentacle ganglion.

nodes.label: Serotonin
nodes.description: Neurotransmitter released by p-CSC discharges in the tentacle ganglion.

nodes.label: Tentacle ganglion
nodes.description: Neural ganglion in which p-CSC discharges release serotonin.

nodes.label: p-VN discharges
nodes.description: Discharges in the p-VN that are suppressed by serotonin in the tentacle ganglion during aversive odor responses.

nodes.label: p-CSC firing rate
nodes.description: Firing-rate property of the posterior cerebral serotonergic cell, reported to decrease when PC oscillation frequency increases after acetylcholine treatment.

nodes.label: Acetylcholine
nodes.description: Cholinergic agent used to increase PC oscillation frequency in the preliminary pharmacological studies.

nodes.label: In vitro conditioning paradigm
nodes.description: In vitro conditioning procedure for examining the neural mechanism by which PC oscillation frequency may mediate odor-guided avoidance behavior.

nodes.label: Odor-guided avoidance behavior
nodes.description: Avoidance behavior whose neural mechanism is discussed in relation to PC oscillation frequency and odor processing.

nodes.label: Aversive odor-induced discharges
nodes.description: Discharges induced by aversive odors and suppressed by serotonin in the tentacle ganglion.
